newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Deals in the market get moving.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Deals in the market get moving.

text.p: Asian debt markets had little new to offer on Wednesday, but some details emerged on issues already in the market.
Standard Chartered Bank's HK$2.0 billion floating rate certificate of deposits issue is doing very well, according to a syndicate manager at the bank.

"Even though the pricing is lower than for our last issue and lower than for Hongkong Bank's last issue, the deal looks like it's headed for a good reception," said Phillip Cracknell, group head of syndicate and asset sales at Standard Chartered.
Seven co-arrangers have joined the deal, which was launched on Monday.

The five-year paper pays a margin of 30 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and an all-in return of 35 basis points. The bank's prior issue launched last July paid 40 basis points all-in.
Hongkong Bank's HK$2.0 billion five-year FRCD set in January paid 38 basis points all-in.
Both issues meet eligibility requirements for use at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Both also qualify for a Hong Kong profits tax concession that cuts levies on gains from debt instruments issued in the territory by half to 8.25 percent if they meet certain requirments.

The Standard Chartered Bank issue, however, has another benefit. Because the bank is headquartered in an OECD country-- Britain--the issue qualifies for a 20 percent, rather than a 100 percent, risk weighting.
Bankers said the issue already is attracting interest from institutional investors that want to buy the paper in the secondary market. These investors benefit most from the tax concession.

Elsewhere, Thailand's SITCA Investment and Securities said its wholly owned unit Metropolis Trust and Securities planned to issue debentures worth up to 3.0 billion baht in both baht and foreign currencies.
A SITCA unit currently is in the market with an asset-backed deal.

In other news from Thailand, the finance ministry said that officials from Moody's Investors Service met with Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Tuesday to review the economic outlook for the country.
Moody's said in mid-February that it might downgrade the senior debt of Thailand as well as that of a number of the country's banks.
